transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-23
Start time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Ellis (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Amir Patel (Redwood CSM); Maya Chen (Aurora Head of MLOps), Liam O'Connor (Aurora CTO), Sofia Alvarez (Aurora DevOps), Ethan Park (Aurora Platform)

Summary (auto): QBR / health check covering usage trends, cost drivers, a reliability incident in May during a burst, and next steps toward a Dedicated/private pilot.

Transcript:
00:00 Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, we're gonna run through the Q2 health check for Aurora Systems, quick intros then we'll jump into usage and costs, priya's gonna run the tech bits.
00:22 Maya: thanks Jordan, hi all, Maya here, I'll hand over to Liam and Sofia for anything procurement/security.
00:30 Priya: hi team, Priya from Redwood, we'll look at p99 latency, KV cache hit rates, and a couple of quick recommendations. I pulled the May burst logs.
00:38 Liam: cool, yeah we've seen a big bump in mid-May, roughly a 3x spike in generation tokens per minute, surprised our cost spiked that much.
01:05 Jordan: yeah the usage is up, Maya, quick qual question — was that from a marketing campaign or organic traffic?
01:18 Maya: marketing campaign plus new feature release we shipped May 10, it changed prompt patterns so more tokens per request.
01:30 Priya: right, that explains it. On the infra side we saw increased KV cache misses because prompt variance grew, so batching dropped efficiency. There's also some queueing during autoscale events.
01:48 Sofia: can you unpack the autoscale part? we thought autoscaling was smoothing things.
02:02 Priya: sure; autoscale works but when the spike is super sharp we spin up nodes, and during warm-up we saw errors — transient 500s — and a momentary p99 latency bump to ~1.4s from baseline ~650ms. The logs show two short windows: May 12 14:22 and May 12 14:47.
02:30 Ethan: those were the ones that tripped our alerting. We have pager noise.
02:40 Jordan: apologies on that noise — we should be able to tighten warm-start and KV cache pre-pop. Recommendation: prefix caching for common templates and configuring pre-warm scaling thresholds.
03:12 Maya: what about cost levers — we want to keep latency sub-1s ideally but costs are increasing.
03:28 Priya: two levers — batching and model quantization profile. For your workload (short-chat style prompts) increasing batching slightly and using an int8 quant profile for non-critical routes drops token cost ~20-30% with <5% quality delta. We can show A/B evals.
03:55 Liam: is quantization fully supported in Redwood Dedicated / Private? we have compliance needs for some datasets.
04:10 Priya: yes — quant profiles are supported across hosted, dedicated and private. for Private we can run quantized models on customer infra; the only caveat is for some edge-case ops we may see small perf deltas, we'll show bench numbers.
04:35 Maya: security — we need SOC2, SSO with our Okta, and KMS integration. Any gaps?
04:50 Amir: we have SOC2 Type II, network diagram, and KMS integration notes. I'll share the pack after this call. We support SAML SSO / Okta and customer-managed KMS/HSM for Private.
05:12 Sofia: good. On Private do you provide the control plane in our VPC or is it hosted?
05:22 Priya: Private can be deployed with a customer-managed control plane in VPC or an on-prem option; we also offer a Private package where control plane sits in customer's cloud account, so logs and audit remain in your environment.
05:40 Liam: that matters for our security team. what's the timeline for a Dedicated trial? procurement wants 30-day pilot.
05:52 Jordan: we can propose a 30-45 day Dedicated trial — reserved capacity — that way you get consistent throughput and we can avoid autoscale warm-up issues for the pilot. We'll include the trial pricing in the quote.
06:12 Maya: excellent. Can you walk through the incident detail quickly? i.e. root cause and remediation?
06:22 Priya: brief — root cause was a combination: sudden prompt variability causing cache misses + scaling laggy due to thresholds. Remediation: immediate was to bump min nodes and aggressive pre-warm during anticipated campaign windows; long term we'll recommend smarter routing and fallback to a cheaper model variant under duress.
06:48 Ethan: fallback — does that change responses noticeably? what about 1% of requests routed to a smaller model?
06:58 Priya: depends on prompt; for templated tasks user won't notice. We can create canary A/B with evaluation suite to measure regressions.
07:20 Jordan: quick demo of cost dashboard points — (link) — shows token split, route costs, and per-model latency slices.
07:45 Maya: we liked the dashboard, can you provide a CSV export of per-route costs?
07:52 Jordan: yes, will include CSV in the follow up.
08:05 Priya: moving to bench numbers — baseline hosted p50~200ms, p99~650ms for your standard prompt size; during the spike p99 hit ~1.4s. On Dedicated with same model and GPU profile we expect p99 <500ms and more predictable throughput.
08:33 Liam: what GPU type?
08:36 Priya: for Dedicated pilot we suggested an A100-like profile; for Private we can also support T4 or H100 depending on cost/perf tradeoffs.
08:52 Maya: cost question again — what's unit token cost delta between Hosted and Dedicated?
09:00 Jordan: as a ballpark, Dedicated committed capacity reduces unit cost by ~25-40% depending on utilization. We'll provide a modeling spreadsheet.
09:20 Maya: great. About the SOC2 docs — can you send those and the network diagram?
09:28 Amir: yes, sending immediately after call.
09:35 Priya: another technical note — KV cache hit rate for you is ~62% during normal ops, dropped to ~38% during the spike due to prompt variance. Improving prompt templates and prefix caching can recover throughput efficiency.
09:57 Sofia: can you give concrete steps? our engineers are willing to implement template normalization.
10:05 Priya: step one: identify high-variance prompts (we can run an analysis and share top 20). step two: implement prefix canonicalization for those routes. step three: tune batching window and min-batch size. we'll help with the config.
10:30 Maya: sounds useful, please run that analysis.
10:36 Jordan: action noted.
10:40 Priya: also recommend a sched for private bench — we should test warm-start scenarios and cold-start to verify autoscale thresholds.
10:55 Liam: ok. Procurement question — what about contract terms for Dedicated trial? any minimums?
11:03 Jordan: trial can be structured as a month of reserved capacity with a reduced rate and option to convert. We'll draft terms and hand to your procurement.
11:18 Maya: timeline? we'd like to kick pilot in July.
11:23 Jordan: feasible — we aim to have quote and SOC2/network pack by Friday (2026-06-25). Pilot could start early July pending procurement.
11:36 Priya: technical deep dive — suggest week of June 29 for SE-led bench and a longer session for platform folks to map telemetry and rollout policy.
11:50 Ethan: that week works for engineers.
12:00 Jordan: any competitors you're evaluating?
12:05 Liam: we're looking at Anthropic for chat models and OpenAI for hosted convenience. Also a bit of Hugging Face for self-hosting.
12:18 Jordan: good to know — we'll highlight our unique inferences: consistent runtime across hosted/dedicated/private, and cost/perf controls like quant profiles and smart routing.
12:35 Maya: one more on data residency — our EU customers' data needs to stay in EU regions only. Do you support region pinning?
12:46 Priya: yes, region pinning is supported on Dedicated and Private; for Hosted we offer region endpoints but Dedicated gives stronger guarantees.
13:00 Sofia: ok team — quick recap and next steps?
13:06 Jordan: recap: 1) Jordan sends cost/usage CSV and quote (due 6/25), 2) Amir shares SOC2 and network/KMS docs (6/24), 3) Priya schedules technical deep dive and private bench (week of 6/29), 4) Maya to confirm stakeholders and pilot approval timeline (6/30).
13:30 Maya: thanks, that works.
13:35 Liam: if we get the quote we'll expedite procurement.
13:40 Jordan: awesome. Any final technical q's?
13:44 Sofia: just one — what's the expected p99 improvement with prefix caching?
13:50 Priya: empirical numbers vary but in similar workloads we saw p99 drop from 650ms to ~420-480ms after prefix canonicalization and improved batching. We'll include those bench artifacts.
14:08 Maya: perfect. Last administrative — can you add procurement and security contacts to the follow up email?
14:16 Jordan: yes, add them to recipients.
14:20 Amir: i'll attach SOC2 and the network diagram.
14:26 Jordan: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with artifacts and the quote.
14:33 (meeting ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-transcriptions — e.g., 'KV cache' appears as 'K V cache' in a few lines; product name 'Redwood Dedicated' transcribed as 'Redwood Dedicate' at one point. Natural speech patterns and filler words retained.
